attempted_claim: Let T and S be invertible measure-preserving rank-one transformations of a standard probability space whose canonical cutting-and-spacer parameters are bounded and which are both totally ergodic. Are T and S necessarily either isomorphic or Furstenberg-disjoint? In particular, if their canonical parameters are not eventually commensurate (no N,M with equal tower heights h_N^{(T)}=h_M^{(S)} and matching cuts and total spacers thereafter), does Furstenberg-disjointness automatically hold?
decisive_failure: The investigation could not establish the target dichotomy in either direction: the proof route lacked the joining-forces-commensurability lemma (explicitly open in Gao-Hill Section 5), and the disproof route had no in-class counterexample construction after rotations, shared eigenvalues, and finite factors were rigorously excluded. The supporting computations cover only small height families and low moduli, and the literature evidence is confined to one fully verified paper plus its cited theorems.
